title: Python continue Statement
learningObjectives: Explain the purpose and behavior of python continue statement.
Write syntactically correct loop code using appropriate indentation.
Trace loop execution for representative inputs.
Select a suitable loop-control statement for a task.
Apply iteration to a practical collection or counting problem.

understand.concept: The continue statement skips the remaining statements in the current loop iteration and proceeds to the next iteration. It does not terminate the loop. In a while loop, ensure that any state needed for progress is updated before continue, or the condition may never change.
understand.whyItMatters: continue is useful when some items should be ignored while the rest of the collection is still processed.
understand.analogy: It is like skipping one item in a checklist and moving to the next item.
understand.analogyLimit: A continue placed before a required counter update in a while loop can accidentally create an infinite loop.

explain.narrative:
## 1. Skip the rest of this iteration

When Python reaches `continue`, it moves to the next iteration of the nearest loop.

## 2. Use with a for loop

It is often used to filter out items that should not be processed.

## 3. Use carefully with while

Update loop state before continue when the update is necessary to reach the stopping condition.
